1 نَضَدَ , aor.
نَضِدَ , (S, K, &c.,) inf. n. نَضْدٌ; (S, L, Msb;) and ↓ نضّد , (L, K,) inf. n. تَنْضِيدٌ; (S, L;) or the latter has an intensive signification; (S, L;) He put goods, household-goods, or commodities, (مَتَاع, S, L, K,) one upon another: (S, L, Msb, K:) or put, or set, them together, (T, A, L,) in regular order, or piled up: (A:) both verbs signify the same: (L, K:) or the latter, he put them one upon another [or side by side] compactly. (S, L.) ―
-b2- [You say,] نَضَدْتُ اللَبِنَ عَلَى المَيِّتِ [I placed the crude bricks in order against the corpse, to support it; as it is laid upon its right side, or so inclined that the face is towards Mekkeh]. (L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
